item.title: 'Legendary' former Liverpool and England star Keegan dies aged 75
item.description:
Former Liverpool and England star Kevin Keegan has died aged 75 after battling cancer, his family announced on Monday.
Keegan, regarded as one of the greatest players of his generation, was diagnosed with stage four cancer and underwent treatment in January.
He became one of only four Englishmen to win the prestigious Ballon d'Or award during a glittering playing career, while his colourful time as a manager included reviving Newcastle.
"It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75," a statement from Keegan's family said.
"Kevin, a double Ballon d'Or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather.
"The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments."
Saluting Keegan's trophy-filled spell at Anfield, Liverpool said: "We are deeply saddened by the passing of the legendary Kevin Keegan and mourn his loss.
"His indomitable spirit and remarkable contribution will be forever etched in our history and his legacy will live on. Rest in peace, Kevin."
The Football Association, posting on the official England X account, said it was "incredibly saddened" by Keegan's death.
Prince William, the Patron of the FA, said: "Incredibly saddened to hear of the passing of Kevin Keegan.
"A truly remarkable footballer and manager who inspired generations with his talent, passion and love of the game."
Keegan, a dynamic striker nicknamed "mighty mouse", won the English top-flight title three times with Liverpool after starting his legendary career with lowly Scunthorpe.
He also won the European Cup in 1977 and the FA Cup in 1974 during an iconic six-year spell on Merseyside before joining German club Hamburg in 1977.
Keegan, who scored 21 goals in 63 games for England, won the Bundesliga title with Hamburg in 1979 and helped them reach the European Cup final the following year.
He was voted the European Player of the Year in 1978 and 1979.
"Rest in peace, 'Mighty Mouse'," Hamburg said as they hailed the "English football icon".
Keegan returned to England to play for Southampton and Newcastle, retiring in 1984 after starring in the Magpies' promotion to the top tier.
"We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply-loved figures in our club's history," Newcastle said in a statement.
"Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.
"Kevin gave supporters hope and pride, and led a team whose style, spirit and passion captured the imagination of football fans around the world. He was so much more than an entertainer."
- 'Will never be forgotten' -
Turning to management in 1992, he led Newcastle to promotion to the Premier League in 1993.
Keegan established them as a force in the top-flight, dubbed "the entertainers" as they finished runners-up to Manchester United after blowing a big lead in 1995-96 title race.
His clashes with United manager Alex Ferguson -- including his famous "I'd love it if we beat them" rant -- took a toll on Keegan, who eventually resigned in 1997.
He went on to manage Fulham before taking charge of England in a turbulent spell from 1999 to 2000, quitting the role of national team boss just hours after a 1-0 defeat against Germany at Wembley.
England had failed to make it out of the group stage at Euro 2000 during Keegan's reign.
Keegan also spent four years as Manchester City manager before finishing his managerial career with a brief return to Newcastle in 2008.
"Kevin was a transformative manager who brought optimism and vibrancy to City during his four-year spell in charge," Manchester City said.
Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said: "RIP Kevin Keegan. One of the greatest players this country has ever produced, trophies and goals galore, double Ballon d'Or winner shows he was an absolute giant of the English game.
"One of the most important men in making Liverpool what it is today."
Former Newcastle and England striker Alan Shearer, who played under Keegan for club and country, paid an emotional tribute to his idol.
"My Hero. My manager. My friend. Sleep easy Boss," he said.

item.title: Spanish king hails World Cup heroes as celebration tour begins
item.description:
Spain's World Cup winners were hailed by the country's king on Monday in Madrid after returning from the United States with the game's most desired trophy in tow.
King Felipe VI and the royal family met the Spanish delegation, led by captain Rodri and coach Luis de la Fuente, at Zarzuela Palace before the players continue their journey into the city with a million fans expected to celebrate with them.
"You have shown your grit, your resilience and your courage, always backed by your technical skill, your control and command of the game, combining head and heart," the king told La Roja's stars, who were dressed in suits.
Spain beat Argentina on Sunday in extra-time thanks to Ferran Torres's strike to clinch their second World Cup, following a first victory in 2010.
The king was joined by Queen Letizia, who wore a red dress to match the colour of the Spanish team's jerseys, and their two daughters, Princess Leonor and Princess Sofia.
Felipe greeted and shook hands with each player, leaning in for a hug with Barcelona's teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.
The king told the players they had been "united" on their "odyssey" to win the expanded 48-team tournament.
The squad is due to meet Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and then take part in an open-top bus parade through central Madrid, where large crowds in national team colours had already gathered.
Spain captain Rodri held the World Cup trophy aloft at the top of the stairs as he descended from the Iberia plane that flew the team home after clinching their second star.
Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in New Jersey on Sunday sparked an outpouring of national pride in the football-mad country.
Many younger supporters were not yet born when Andres Iniesta's extra-time goal against the Netherlands secured Spain's first World Cup in South Africa 16 years ago.
On Monday morning, the Castellana, Madrid's main avenue, bore the marks of a boozy evening -- the tarmac strewn with trash, beer cans and shards of glass.
Among the last remaining supporters, some slept with grins on their faces on the pavement or on benches, while others were still staggering home as cleaning crews worked from the early hours to prepare the route for tonight's party.
Spain's World Cup winners bus parade starts at the Prime Minister's residence Moncloa before heading to Cibeles square.
A ceremony involving the players will then be held at the square, the traditional gathering point for celebrations by the Spanish national team and its supporters.
Some fans, who already had only a short night's sleep, are planning to celebrate again, like Bruno Gonzalez del Yerro, a 32-year-old financier.
"We'll have to celebrate it one way or another, given that it only happens every four years and that Spain hadn't won it for about (sixteen) years now -- it definitely deserves a party," he said.
- Both trophies -
Spain's women's side won the World Cup in 2023, meaning for the first time a country has both trophies at the same time.
In 2030 Spain will defend their crown on home soil, as one of the World Cup hosts along with Portugal and Morocco.
The Spanish press was running out of superlatives to describe its heroes after they overcame favourites France in the semi-finals before downing Argentina.
"The kings of all-time!" wrote Marca, celebrating a "second star that will now be stitched onto the Spanish jersey after yet another masterclass in collective play."
On a tragic note, a 13-year-old boy was killed around midnight in the town of Ciudad Rodrigo in the west, after a fountain crumbled under the weight of supporters who had climbed onto it to celebrate Spain's victory.
Argentina, despite the presence of all-time great Lionel Messi, failed to create clear chances against Spain's well-organised and more positive side in the final.
Enzo Fernandez's red card left Argentina with their backs pinned to the wall and Barcelona forward Torres slammed home after fellow substitute Nico Williams teed him up.
"It's not my goal, it's the goal of 47 million people," said Spain's match-winner.
Messi had a sensational World Cup but drifted through the final like a ghost, shedding tears at the end. In Madrid, tears will also flow on Monday night, but tears of joy.

item.title: Thousands welcome home Argentina squad, without Messi, despite World Cup loss
item.description:
Thousands of fans braved the cold and rain Monday to give a rapturous welcome to the Argentine football squad who landed back home without star Lionel Messi, after their World Cup final loss to Spain.
It was not the homecoming Argentines had hoped for, four years after millions celebrated their team's tournament victory in 2022, but fresh scenes of joyful chaos filled the street as they danced, sang and set off fireworks to thank the players.
The Argentine Football Association (AFA) said earlier that some squad members would not be on the flight, and iconic team captain Messi was not seen descending from the aircraft in images broadcast on local television.
Coach Lionel Scaloni and the rest of the team were welcomed with a red carpet outside the aircraft and a military band.
They then boarded a bus, waving to frenzied fans along the way.
Despite falling short of a second straight championship, "Argentines will celebrate anyway," said housewife Marga Ledezma. The 36-year-old thanked Messi for "all the years he made us happy," urging him not to quit playing for Argentina, but admitting this would be difficult as he was 39.
Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in a game that has been criticized in international media for a plethora of fouls and displays of poor sportsmanship from the Albiceleste.
"I think they criticize us because we know what it's like to suffer, that we get up, we fall down again, and we keep going," said Ledezma.
Many fans highlighted that the real victory for Argentina was the 2-1 semi-final win over England, played against the backdrop of a lingering dispute between the countries over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.
Some carried flags declaring "The Falklands are Argentine." FIFA is investigating the Argentine team after players held up a banner bearing the phrase after their win against England which sparked a backlash from London.
- 'The pain is immense' -
"This team united us all, and we should be grateful for that. We will always be there for them, rain or shine. I would say thank you to Messi and that he gave it his all," said Leonardo Barrientos, 36, who works in a textile workshop.
Maria Ortiz, 28, came to welcome the team with her two-year-old, and said Spain "deserved the win" but she was "happy for what the team gave us."
Messi wrote on Instagram on Monday that "the pain is immense and it's going to take a long time for this wound to heal."
"I'll also hold on to all the good memories," he wrote alongside a photo of himself. "Today it's hard to appreciate what we achieved, but this squad reached two consecutive World Cup finals."
With the tournament over, President Javier Milei announced that a future date agreed with the team would be set as a public holiday to celebrate their performance in the World Cup. No further details have been announced.
While crestfallen after the loss, thousands of Argentines headed to the traditional celebration point at the Obelisk in Buenos Aires where they partied for hours on Sunday evening.
Late at night, brief clashes broke out at the monument and police used water cannons, tear gas, and rubber bullets to disperse revellers. Fifteen people were detained, according to police sources.

item.title: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi protest outside Modi's house
item.description:
Indian opposition leaders Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka, along with members of their Congress party, staged a protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's house, videos shared by the party showed on Tuesday.

"We have marched to PM Modi’s house to demand answers from him for the brutalities against young students yesterday," Rahul Gandhi posted on X, referring to the clashes between youth protesters and police in Delhi on Monday.

The Congress protest followed a police crackdown on a youth-led movement that has grown rapidly over allegations of examination paper leaks, unemployment and government accountability.

Indian media reports, Rahul Gandhi said the march was aimed at demanding answers from the prime minister. He also called on Modi to apologise to the protesters, accusing the government of failing India's youth and suppressing peaceful dissent.

In a notable development, union Minister Jitendra Singh later visited the protest site and held talks with Rahul Gandhi, signalling the government's first direct political outreach to the opposition after the confrontation.

While no agreement was announced, the meeting suggested an attempt to ease tensions as pressure mounted on the government.

Prime Minister Modi, addressing Parliament, defended his government's handling of the examination scandal, saying those responsible had been arrested and promising a "foolproof" examination system.

The youth movement has vowed to continue its campaign despite ongoing dialogue with the government.

item.title: Bangladeshi internal audit professional receives ACIIA OCIA award
item.description:
Nausheen Ahmed, head of Internal Audit and Compliance at BRAC University and secretary general of The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) Bangladesh, has received the Outstanding Contribution in the Field of Internal Auditing (OCIA) Award 2026 from the Asian Confederation of Institutes of Internal Auditors (ACIIA). She is the first Bangladeshi to receive this honour.

The award was presented to her on 19 June 2026 at the ACIIA Business Meeting and 20th Foundation Anniversary Programme in Singapore. She was recognised for her outstanding leadership, innovative initiatives and long-term contributions to the internal auditing profession at organisational, national, regional and global levels, reports a press release.

The OCIA Award is one of ACIIA's highest professional honours, presented in recognition of exceptional contributions to leadership, professional development, research, education and the advancement of the internal auditing profession.

ACIIA is the second-largest regional confederation of The Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA), after North America. It represents Institutes of Internal Auditors across Asia and plays a significant role in promoting international standards, knowledge-sharing and professional excellence.

With more than 13 years of experience in internal auditing, corporate governance, risk management and compliance, Nausheen Ahmed has served in key roles at ACI Limited, Marico Bangladesh, ASA International and BRAC University. Throughout her career, she has worked to establish internal auditing as a more strategic, value-driven and impactful profession.

One of her most significant contributions to internal audit education in Bangladesh has been bringing BRAC University into The IIA Academic Alliance Programme. As a result, the university became the first educational institution in Bangladesh to incorporate internal auditing into its curriculum.

Later, through her initiative, United International University also joined the same international programme. This has created a sustainable foundation for developing future internal audit professionals in the country while strengthening collaboration between academia and the profession.

At the national level, Nausheen Ahmed has set a new benchmark as the youngest and the first woman to serve as secretary general of IIA Bangladesh. Under her leadership, member engagement, professional capability and the institute's visibility at both national and international levels have increased significantly.

Her initiatives, including specialised training, knowledge-sharing activities and professional development programmes, have also led to a notable rise in participation among internal audit professionals.

She has also played a key role in developing the next generation of internal auditors. Her Risk-Based Internal Audit training module and practical case studies have already benefited more than 120 professionals. In addition, she has been mentoring professionals from Bangladesh and other countries in obtaining internationally recognised certifications, including the Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) qualification.

Nausheen Ahmed's contributions have earned international recognition beyond Bangladesh. As a member of The IIA's Exam Development Committee, she has reviewed more than 1,000 CIA examination questions and played an important role in updating the syllabuses for the CIA and CIA Challenge examinations.

She has also contributed to developing key professional guidance, including Communicating Final Engagement Results and Third-Party Topical Requirement, as a member of The IIA Advisory Group and the Global Task Force.

In 2025, she participated as an invited speaker at The IIA International Conference in Toronto, Canada, and The IIA ERM Virtual Conference, where she delivered presentations on the evolving role of internal auditing, enterprise risk management, crisis management and strategic governance.

Earlier, in 2020, she was selected by The IIA Global as one of its Top 15 Emerging Leaders, recognising her leadership potential and contributions to the profession.

item.title: Zia assassination: Mozaffar Hossain has to be produced at Tribunal
item.description:
Former military officer Mozzaffar Hossain, arrested on charges of involvement in the assassination of former President Ziaur Rahman, has been ordered to be produced before the International Crimes Tribunal.

The Bangladesh Army has been instructed to present him by 10 AM on Thursday.

Major (Retd.) Mozzaffar Hossain (77) had been a fugitive for 45 years. On Wednesday night, the police’s detective branch announced his arrest from a house in Banani, the capital. The next day, Thursday, he was handed over to the military police at Dhaka Cantonment.

Ziaur Rahman assassination: Mozaffar's role and 45 years in hiding

The three-member International Crimes Tribunal-2, led by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, ordered today, Tuesday, that Mozzaffar Hossain be presented before the International Crimes Tribunal.

The other two members of the tribunal are Judge Md Manjurul Bashed and Judge Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir.

The tribunal issued this order following an application by the Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal, Md Aminul Islam.

The Chief Prosecutor stated in the tribunal that the accused, Mozzaffar Hossain, is currently in military custody.

Zia assassination: How Major Mozzaffar was identified

The tribunal stated in the order that for an effective and proper investigation, it is necessary to produce Mozzaffar Hossain before the tribunal in this case of crimes against humanity.

On the early morning of 30 May 1981, a group of misguided military officers brutally assassinated then-President Ziaur Rahman at the Chittagong Circuit House.

Ziaur Rahman, the founder of the BNP, had gone to Chattogram (Then spelt Chittagong) the previous day to resolve a local party dispute.

According to various historical accounts, narratives, or books published about the assassination of Ziaur Rahman, Mozzaffar was one of the armed military officers who went to the Chittagong Circuit House on the morning of 30 May 1981.

45 years since Zia's assassination: The blood-stained dawn at Circuit House and an unfinished history

He was close to Zia at the moment of the assassination. After the assassination of Ziaur Rahman, Mozzaffar fled. A reward was announced for his capture at the time.

Following Zia’s assassination, 18 military officers were tried in a military court on charges of ‘rebellion''.

Among them, 13 were sentenced to death, and others received various terms of imprisonment. However, Major SM Khaled and Major Mozzaffar successfully managed to escape.

item.title: Measles claims nearly 800 children in 4 months
item.description:
Four more children have died in the country due to measles symptoms in the last 24 hours (from 8 AM Monday to 8 AM Tuesday).

Some 797 children have lost their lives to measles and its symptoms since 15 March, over a period of more than four months.

This information has been reported in the measles-related report of the Directorate General of Health Services today, Tuesday.

On 26 June, the death toll of children due to measles and its symptoms exceeded 700. Within 26 days, the death toll is approaching 800.

Among the four children who died in the last 24 hours, two were from Sylhet, one from Rajshahi, and one from Mymensingh.

In the last 24 hours, 1,008 children have been affected by measles and its symptoms.

Among them, 130 children have been diagnosed with measles. Since 15 March, over a period of more than four months, 134,156 children have been affected by measles and its symptoms.

Among these, 14,708 children have been diagnosed with measles.

According to the information from the Directorate General of Health Services, since 15 March of this year, 102,244 children have been admitted to hospitals with measles symptoms.

Among them, 98,411 children have recovered and returned home.

item.title: Why did Messi tell his teammates to 'forget everything' before the final?
item.description:
SOCCER-WORLDCUP-ESP-ARG/

A video circulating on social media has sparked debate over Lionel Messi's final pre-match words to his Argentina teammates before the World Cup final.

Argentine media have picked up the story, with many questioning why Messi—who had posted an emotional message on Instagram before the match—urged his teammates to "forget everything" as they walked out of the dressing room.

According to TyC Sports, the viral footage shows the Argentina captain addressing the squad before they took the field.

"Everyone, stay calm. The important thing is that we remain calm."

Up to that point, nothing seemed unusual. But it was his next words that drew widespread attention on social media, "Let's forget everything. Let's just play. Let's focus only on the game."

The video shows Messi standing at the dressing room entrance while delivering the message, with his teammates appearing composed. Still, many have wondered what exactly he wanted Enzo Fernández, Emiliano Martínez and the rest of the squad to "forget."

While it remains unclear what the 39-year-old was referring to, Argentina had come under criticism before the final. Spain had accused the reigning champions of receiving favourable refereeing decisions during the tournament.

Before the final, Spain defender Aymeric Laporte said some refereeing decisions in recent matches had been genuinely surprising, with certain incidents going unpunished.

"Especially with Argentina. They're a team that likes to leave a mark on their opponents. That sort of thing shouldn't be allowed in football, particularly in major competitions, because it can unsettle you and make you angry," Laporte said.

Argentina eventually lost 1-0 to Spain in the final in New Jersey, ending their title defence and handing Spain its first World Cup triumph in 16 years.

Although the refereeing itself was not a major talking point during the match, tensions flared after the final whistle, with several Argentina players and members of the coaching staff clashing with Spanish players.

Following the ugly scenes, FIFA has launched an investigation into the post-match confrontation.

item.title: Arrogance or pride? Argentina grapples with World Cup villain label
item.description:
ARGENTINA-FBL-WC-2026

Critics blasted Argentina for dirty tactics and poor sportsmanship during their 1-0 loss to Spain, cementing the country's status as World Cup villain that grew throughout the tournament.

But Argentines argue they are just passionate and misunderstood.

"I think we deserve some credit for not being very well-liked, because of this tendency to be arrogant and look down on most people from a pedestal," said Leo Simone, 55, a lawyer, from his home north of Buenos Aires.

"They confuse arrogance with pride," his wife chimed in, preferring not to give her name.

While star Lionel Messi is beloved around the world, anti-Argentina sentiment grew as critics argued they were FIFA's darling and received favorable referee calls such as penalties and cards shown to opponents.

Then came the final, replete with fouls, brawls on the pitch, and the Argentine squad turning their backs when Spain received the World Cup trophy.

Why Argentina are the World Cup's favourite villains

The New York Times called it a "tetchy, petulant and distasteful performance."

Former Germany player Thomas Hitzlsperger wrote on X that the team were "disgusting sportsmen" and British television personality Piers Morgan said "they basically just went around whacking as many Spanish players as they could."

Near Ezeiza Airport, where thousands of fans welcomed the players returning to Buenos Aires on Monday night, Maximiliano Heredia, a 35-year-old construction worker, said, "We've always been criticised, we're used to it. But we always give it our all."

'We love it'

Many Argentines online wore the criticism as a badge of honor.

"There's something about Argentine irreverence that they can't tolerate. Our rebelliousness irritates them, enrages them...they call us cocky, cheaters, dirty. And we love it, it fills us with pride," journalist Pedro Rosemblat wrote on his Instagram.

Sports journalist Ezequiel Fernandez Moores told AFP that some criticism was justified, "Sometimes we think we're the center of the universe, that God and our own navel are Argentine."

Thousands welcome home Argentina squad, without Messi, despite World Cup loss

He said local football codes of provocation, mockery, and boasting did not translate to a global audience.

"We can't expect the world to understand us, our way of being, feeling, and expressing ourselves," he said.

Nevertheless, the team turning their backs on Spain as they received the cup was "not right," he said.

The lawyer Simone rejects the notion that physical play makes Argentina a violent team.

"Argentina is a team that fights hard, like almost all South American football, but Spain also resorted to tactical fouls," he said. "It's football: if you don't like being hit, play volleyball."

For Evelio Rubio, a 47-year-old Venezuelan neurologist who has lived in Argentina for a decade, it is impossible to understand from outside how "football is experienced here."

For a Venezuelan accustomed to his national team not winning titles, experiencing that passion from within "is spectacular."

Racism accusations

Argentine fans and some players have also faced accusations of racism -- such as a chant sung by the team in the past mocking the Black players on the French team as not being really French.

'The last of Messi': Argentines mourn loss and end of an era

There is also a long history of club-level fans throwing bananas on the field or making monkey gestures at Brazilian fans or black players.

During this World Cup, FIFA condemned racism in a statement after an Argentine supporter told a Black US influencer known as IShowSpeed to go "cry at the zoo" during a livestream.

American actor Samuel L Jackson stirred controversy when he urged black people in an Instagram story not to support Argentina which he dubbed one of "the most racist countries in the world."

Sociologist Ivan Schuliaquer of the National University of San Martin said people should not take racism related to football and apply it generally to Argentine society and history.

This racism exists and should not be denied, he said.

"But, in many cases, these labels come from colonising countries that have not yet fully resolved the issue of racism."

item.title: CNG station owners threaten nationwide shutdown on July 30
item.description:
The Bangladesh CNG Filling Station and Conversion Workshop Owners Association has announced a nationwide shutdown of CNG filling stations from 6am to 12 midnight on July 30, demanding an increase in the commission on compressed natural gas (CNG) sales.
The association also warned that if its demands are not met, CNG filling stations across the country will remain closed indefinitely from August 23.
The announcement was made at a press conference held at Akram Tower in the capital's Bijoynagar on Tuesday.
Reading out a written statement, Steering Committee Convener Amiruzzaman Chowdhury said all CNG filling stations would remain closed on July 30 while discussions with the government continue.
"If our demands remain unmet, CNG filling stations across the country will shut down indefinitely from August 23," he said.
Association leaders said the commission on CNG sales has remained unchanged at Tk8 per cubic metre since September 1, 2015, despite a sharp rise in inflation, workers' wages, equipment prices, bank charges, lease fees for Roads and Highways Department land and various government licence fees over the past 11 years.
They demanded that the commission be increased to Tk13.96 per cubic metre, an increase of Tk5.96 from the current rate.
The association also called for an automatic adjustment of the commission whenever gas prices are increased in the future. It urged the government to stop requiring additional security deposits from existing customers following gas price hikes and to rationalise lease fees charged by the Roads and Highways Department, as well as licence fees imposed by different government agencies.
The owners said that, under previous government commitments, the commission should have increased by Tk3.30 in line with gas price adjustments and by another Tk2.46 following eight hikes in electricity tariffs. Combined, they argued, their justified commission should have reached Tk13.10 per cubic metre at the beginning of 2024.
The association's general secretary added that a further 19% increase in electricity prices in June had raised operating costs by an additional Tk0.86 per cubic metre. He said the demand for a commission of Tk13.96 was based solely on government recommendations, inflation and higher electricity costs, without factoring in other rising operational expenses.
Association leaders said they had submitted letters outlining their demands to the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) and the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources but received no response. They also failed to secure a meeting with the adviser concerned.
As a result, they convened an emergency general meeting on Saturday and formed a 12-member steering committee, which subsequently decided to announce the shutdown program.

item.title: Heavy rains push vegetable prices above Tk100 in Dhaka
item.description:
Prolonged rainfall and heavy downpours have disrupted the supply of vegetables to Dhaka's kitchen markets, triggering a sharp rise in prices. Over the past few days, the prices of most vegetables have climbed by Tk20 to Tk40 per kilogram, pushing many above the Tk100 mark. The weather-induced supply crunch has also driven up the prices of fish, eggs and chicken, adding to consumers' grocery bills.
Traders attributed the price hike to delayed shipments from different parts of the country and reduced production caused by heavy rainfall, which damaged vegetable fields in several areas. The resulting supply shortage has pushed up prices.
After visiting several kitchen markets in the capital, it was found that long eggplants are being sold at Tk100 per kg, while round eggplants cost Tk150. Bitter gourd is priced between Tk100 and Tk120 per kg, pointed gourd and okra Tk70-Tk80, ridge gourd Tk90-Tk100, snake gourd Tk70-Tk80, and cucumber Tk120-Tk130 per kg.
Bottle gourd, which sold for Tk60 just a few days ago, now costs Tk90-Tk100 each. Green chilli prices have also climbed, with ordinary varieties selling for Tk160-Tk180 per kg and premium-quality chillies reaching Tk200. Carrots are being sold at Tk160 per kg, while tomatoes are priced between Tk120 and Tk160.
Prices of onions and garlic have also increased. Onions, previously sold at Tk40 per kg, now cost Tk60, while garlic has risen to Tk140 per kg.
Eggs and chicken also cost more
Alongside vegetables, egg and poultry prices have also increased. Duck eggs are selling at Tk70 per four, while farm-produced brown eggs are priced at Tk45-Tk48 per four. Broiler chicken is selling for Tk190-Tk200 per kg, while Sonali chicken costs Tk340-Tk360 per kg.
Fish prices remain high
Fish prices have also remained high. Medium-sized farmed rui and katla are selling for Tk400-Tk450 per kg, up from Tk350-Tk380 a few days ago. Telapia is priced at Tk240-Tk260 per kg, pangas Tk220-Tk250, pabda Tk400-Tk450, tengra Tk900, and farmed shrimp Tk900-Tk1,200 per kg.
Hilsa supply has also declined, with one-kilogram fish selling for Tk1,600-Tk2,400 each.
Traders blame weather-related supply disruptions
Altaf Hossain, a fish trader at Narinda Market, said prolonged rainfall and flooding had reduced fish supplies. "We are paying higher prices at the wholesale market, which is reflected in retail prices. Prices are expected to ease once supply returns to normal," he said.
Abu Sayeed, a vegetable trader at Ray Saheb Bazar, said continuous rainfall had disrupted vegetable deliveries to the capital, while crop damage in several regions further reduced supply.
"If the weather improves, prices are likely to decline gradually," he added.
Shoppers feel the pinch
A customer at Narinda Market said the combined impact of persistent rainfall and flooding in several regions had significantly increased vegetable prices.
"Daily grocery shopping now costs much more than before. People will get some relief only when supplies return to normal," the shopper said.

item.title: SG: Comparison between BIMSTEC, SAARC misleading
item.description:
Secretary General of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Indra Mani Pandey on Tuesday said the comparison between BIMSTEC and the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) is "misleading and misplaced," and it hurts the interests of BIMSTEC.
"My request has always been that BIMSTEC's vision be appreciated in its own right, and it should not be seen in the context of any other organisation, which has its own history and achievements," he said while responding to a question during an interaction with the members of the Diplomatic Correspondents Association, Bangladesh (DCAB) at the BIMSTEC headquarters.
He said BIMSTEC is poised to emerge as a leading regional organisation in the Indo-Pacific, noting that the regional grouping has made significant institutional progress since its establishment in 1997, evolving into a stronger platform for cooperation between South Asia and Southeast Asia.
Pandey said BIMSTEC was created to bring the two regions closer through practical and tangible cooperation, particularly in technical and economic fields.
"BIMSTEC enjoys the requisite political support of its members, focuses on forging tangible cooperation and stays away from political issues," said the BIMSTEC chief, noting that BIMSTEC is undergoing reforms and revitalisation in order to make it an efficient, effective and dynamic regional organisation.
He said the organisation has achieved notable milestones over the years, including the adoption of its Charter, the development of institutional mechanisms and the formulation of a long-term vision document, reflecting its growing maturity as a regional organisation.
The secretary general said discussions should now focus not only on BIMSTEC's achievements but also on its future direction, including whether the grouping should broaden its agenda and deepen cooperation in additional sectors to address emerging regional challenges.
Regional cooperation is a prerequisite for the development and security of the Bay of Bengal region, and BIMSTEC has emerged as a dynamic and suitable platform to realise it, he said.
The secretary general said BIMSTEC serves the core security and developmental interests of Bangladesh as well as other member states. "BIMSTEC is a real and present opportunity, not a remote and hypothetical possibility."
Talking about challenges, the secretary general said Bangladesh faces similar security and developmental challenges as other BIMSTEC member states, which it cannot deal with alone.
The agenda of BIMSTEC, which has evolved with the active participation of Bangladesh, reflects the country's developmental priorities, he said.
Bangladesh leads regional cooperation in key sectors—trade, investment and development, fiscal and monetary policy, as well as the blue economy.
"The success in forging regional cooperation through BIMSTEC will contribute, directly and indirectly, to the realisation of a developed, secure and prosperous Bangladesh," said the BIMSTEC chief.
Bangladesh is the current chair of BIMSTEC. It assumed the chairmanship at the conclusion of the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok in April 2025.
The secretary general said Bangladesh has been committed to regional cooperation through BIMSTEC, based on its belief that regional cooperation contributes to its development.
Pandey said BIMSTEC is engaged in negotiations on a "BIMSTEC Motor Vehicles Agreement," which will facilitate land connectivity among the member states.
India has proposed establishing a "BIMSTEC Sustainable Maritime Transport Centre" in the country.
Pandey said it has been decided to institutionalise the BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting to strengthen and deepen regional cooperation on security. The inaugural meeting of the home ministers is scheduled to be hosted by India in October 2026.
He said the BIMSTEC Plan of Action (PoA) on countering radicalisation and terrorism has been finalised, and an "action matrix" to implement it is under consideration.
Pandey said an action matrix for implementing the finalised Plan of Action to combat human trafficking has been developed.
He said BIMSTEC is also considering measures to enhance the ease of travel, including visa facilitation, and is considering a BIMSTEC visa facilitation scheme.

item.title: Man to die for killing wife in Dhaka
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday convicted a man and sentenced him to death for killing his wife in 2017.
Judge of the Dhaka Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court-6, Sadekin Habib Bappi, handed down the judgment.
The convict is identified as Monir Hossain, a resident of the Badda area in the capital.
According to the prosecution, Monir Hossain married Shakila Khatun Shoma in 2003. The couple had one daughter.
Shoma was repeatedly pressured to bring money from her family. Over time, her family paid Monir Tk11 lakh.
On October 6, 2017, Monir had an altercation with his wife over the issue and at one stage, he slit Shoma's throat with a sharp weapon, leaving her critically injured.
She was later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared her dead.
Shoma's mother, Akter Banu, filed a case with Badda Police Station.
Police arrested Monir, who later gave a confessional statement admitting his guilt.
On December 7, 2017, police submitted a chargesheet against Monir.
After examining records and 15 witnesses, the court handed down the punishment.

Bangladesh aims to be trusted global source of green jute solutions
item.description:
The government on Tuesday expressed its firm commitment to working together to transform the jute sector into a modern industry, ensure fair prices for farmers, and establish Bangladesh as a trusted global source of climate-friendly jute-based solutions. To achieve these goals, a coordination meeting titled “Strategic Economic Diplomacy and Export Expansion for Bangladesh’s Jute Sector” was jointly organised in Dhaka by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Textiles and Jute.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam and State Minister for Textiles and Jute Md Shariful Alam announced the formation of a joint working group between the two ministries and the organisation of an ‘International Jute Expo’ in the near future with a renewed global outlook.
Secretaries of both ministries, senior government officials, and representatives from the Department of Jute, the jute industry, research institutions, and development partner organisations attended the meeting.
The state minister for foreign affairs reaffirmed the government's commitment to revitalising the jute sector and underscored the importance of organising Jute and Jute Products Exhibitions to restore the glory of the country's "golden fibre."
She placed particular emphasis on leveraging economic diplomacy, with the active support of Bangladesh missions abroad, to promote the development of the jute industry.
The state minister for textiles and jute expressed appreciation to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for taking this important initiative and highlighted the need for close coordination between the two ministries and the private sector to enhance jute production, processing, value addition, and market diversification.
The meeting decided that the proposed joint working group would formulate a national roadmap for jute exhibitions, address trade barriers affecting the jute industry, facilitate the establishment of dedicated research centres for jute, promote the adoption of modern technologies across the sector, and monitor the progress of mill modernisation initiatives.
It was also decided that the proposed International Jute Expo would bring together domestic and international buyers, researchers, and investors to strengthen Bangladesh's engagement with global markets. The meeting also discussed the establishment of mandatory jute display centres and gift shops at Bangladesh's international airports, the expedited implementation of a project to introduce jute-made school bags for primary school students, and achieving full self-sufficiency in jute seed production within the next three years by reducing import dependence through increased domestic production.

item.title: ICT orders army to produce retired major Muzaffar on Thursday
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT)-2 on Tuesday ordered the authorities to produce Major (retd) Mozaffar Hossain, an accused in the assassination case of Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, before the tribunal on Thursday.
The ICT-2, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, passed the order, allowing a plea filed by the Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam.
"The arrested Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, an accused in a crimes against humanity case linked to the July Mass Uprising (miscellaneous case), has involvement in various crimes against humanity dating back to the 'One-Eleven' period. Major (retd) Mozaffar also had conversations and other links with Masud Uddin Chowdhury. These connections should be probed. Therefore, we sought a production warrant to interrogate him, and the tribunal granted our prayer," the chief prosecutor said.
The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested Major (Retd) Md Mozaffar Hossain from the capital's DOHS area on July 15.
He was later handed over to Military Police at Dhaka Cantonment.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Next generation should learn positive use of technology
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj on Tuesday said that instead of fearing the advancement of digital technology, the next generation should be built through safe and responsible use of technology.
“Advancement of technology is an ongoing process, Therefore, instead of keeping children and adolescents away from technology, we must prepare them for the future by teaching them its proper use,” he said.
He made the remarks while addressing as the chief guest at a national learning exchange programme on Digital Gender Norms (Gender-Based Social Norms in the Digital Space), organised by BBC Media Action at a hotel in the capital, said a press release.
The state minister said although attempts were made to silence the people's voice by shutting down the internet during the July Mass Uprising of 2024, those efforts did not succeed.
He said experience proved that digital platforms have become an inseparable part of society, the state and citizens' lives. Therefore, he added, the most important task now is not to reject technology but to build the capacity to use it properly.
Mentioning that there is now a clear mismatch between technological advancement and the prevailing social and cultural values, he said to bridge this gap, the education sector, families, society and the state must work together.
He stressed the need to train children and adolescents on safe digital behaviour, information verification and online ethics. Bobby Hajjaj said fake images, fake videos, character assassination and digital harassment on social media have reached an alarming level.
Women, adolescent girls and women politicians are the worst victims of such abuse. Therefore, he said, effective implementation of laws and policies is now essential to ensure accountability on digital platforms and protect children and women.
He said the government's objective is not to create unreasonable barriers in the use of technology but to establish a balance between freedom and security.
He, however, also expressed the opinion that effective regulation is necessary in some cases to ensure the safety of children and women in the current social context.
The state minister said the government is incorporating value-based education, digital safety, life skills, gender sensitivity and civic values as important components of the new primary education curriculum.
He said coordinated efforts are underway with local and foreign experts and various development partners, including UNESCO, to achieve this goal.
He said the new education system includes plans to gradually introduce interactive digital classroom facilities, provide tablets to teachers and, in the future, education-friendly digital devices to students to bring both teachers and learners under technology-based education.
Bobby Hajjaj said ensuring the safe development of children is not only the responsibility of parents but also the responsibility of society as a whole. To this end, community engagement is being strengthened at primary schools.
Guardian committees have already been formed to oversee the school meal programme, while initiatives have also been taken to involve parents and local communities in other areas of the education system, he added.
Addressing development partners as well as international and national NGOs, he said the government is ready to adopt and expand any initiative that proves effective for students. "Our ministry is now working under an open-door policy. Bring us effective initiatives, and we will evaluate them and try to implement them on a larger scale," he said.
Referring to women's empowerment, the state minister said establishing women's leadership requires more than slogans. Equal opportunities, equal rights, a safe environment and self-confidence must be ensured from childhood.
He said the foundation for this transformation must be built in educational institutions.

item.title: EC reviews local government election laws ahead of October polls
item.description:
The Election Commission (EC) is holding a meeting to finalise proposed amendments to local government election laws and the electoral code of conduct ahead of the next phase of local government polls.
The meeting began on Tuesday at the Election Building in Agargaon, Dhaka, chaired by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) AMM Nasir Uddin.
The four other election commissioners and relevant EC officials are also attending.
According to EC officials, the meeting is expected to finalize proposals related to candidate eligibility, campaign regulations, penalties for violations of the code of conduct and other key electoral issues.
Sources said the commission may approve recommendations to be sent to the government for amending the laws governing city corporations, municipalities, upazila parishads, district councils and union parishads. Amendments to the Union Parishad Election Code of Conduct are also likely to be approved.
Under the proposed code, candidates or their election agents could be declared immediately disqualified through a written order in cases of serious violations of electoral rules.
The draft amendments also include proposals to shorten the campaign period, impose restrictions on electioneering through social media and regulate the use of microphones and sound systems during campaigns.
The EC is additionally considering expanding the list of disqualified candidates. The draft proposes barring MPO-listed educational institution teachers, dual citizens, loan defaulters and guarantors of defaulted loans from contesting local government elections.
The proposals also include increasing the amount of election security deposits for candidates and removing the existing requirement for independent candidates to collect signatures from 1% of voters in the constituency.
Earlier, the Election Commission indicated that the local government election process could begin with Union Parishad polls in the first half of October. The schedule is expected to be announced by the end of August.
As part of election preparations, the EC says ballot boxes, election materials and the necessary manpower have been kept ready for the upcoming polls.

item.title: Rizvi questions who sheltered Zia assassination convict for 45 years
item.description:
BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Tuesday raised questions over who had sheltered and patronized one of the convicted killers of former president Ziaur Rahman for the past 45 years.
He raised the question while speaking as the chief guest at a program to pray for the departed soul of the party's former vice-president Zakir Hossain Nannu organized by Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal in Dhaka's Naya Paltan.
Rizvi said the arrest proved that no criminal ultimately escapes justice.
"But the question is where was he during these 45 years? Who gave him shelter? Who maintained him? Who patronized him?" he asked.
Rizvi said many developments have taken place following the events of August 15, 1975, adding that some of those who later became ministers were also associated with Awami League. "Anyway, I am not going into those issues now," he said.
Encouraging party leaders and activists not to lose hope, Rizvi said people should rely on hard work rather than frustration.
"Don't believe in frustration, believe in your hard work," he said, urging everyone to remain committed to their ideals.
He said no one's hard work ever goes in vain and that even if some people leave this world without seeing the results of their struggle, their memories inspire others to continue working.
Rizvi said the sacrifices of leaders like Zakir Hossain Nannu would be meaningful if these initiatives achieved success over the coming years.
Rizvi said that from the anti-Ershad movement to the past 17 years of movement under Begum Khaleda Zia and Tarique Rahman, the party consistently fought for democracy.
Despite repeated conspiracies and challenges, he added, the BNP has never resorted to compromise or secret deals.
Among others, BNP Joint Secretary General Advocate Abdus Salam Azad, Organizing Secretary for Volunteers Affairs Mir Sarafat Ali Sapu, Jubo Dal President Abdul Monayem Munna and General Secretary Nurul Islam Nayon attended the program.

item.title: PROGGA, ATMA call for complete ban on nicotine pouches in Bangladesh
item.description:
PROGGA (Knowledge for Progress) and the Anti-Tobacco Media Alliance (ATMA) have called for a complete ban on nicotine pouches in Bangladesh, expressing alarm over the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution's (BSTI) move to formulate standards for the product.
In a joint statement issued on Tuesday, the two organizations said the technical committee formed by BSTI includes representatives of tobacco companies but excludes the National Tobacco Control Cell (NTCC) and tobacco control organizations. They argued that the involvement of tobacco companies violates Article 5.3 of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC).
Nicotine pouches pose a serious threat to public health. Although tobacco companies promote these products as “relatively less harmful,” the World Health Organization (WHO) has clearly warned that, despite containing no tobacco leaf, nicotine pouches deliver high levels of nicotine. This highly addictive substance can impair brain development in children and adolescents and increase the risks of cardiovascular disease and other health complications. According to the WHO, adolescents and young adults are emerging as the largest consumers of these emerging tobacco products worldwide. To protect public health and prevent nicotine addiction among young people, at least 16 countries, including Singapore, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Russia, have already imposed complete ban on nicotine pouches.
Commenting on the issue, ABM Zubair, executive director of PROGGA, said: “Although the Ministry of Health had proposed a ban on nicotine pouches, it was not incorporated into the amended tobacco control law. Efforts are now under way to introduce and market the product in Bangladesh. Bangladesh should follow the example of other countries and impose a complete ban on nicotine pouches.”
It is noteworthy that Hon'ble Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has already unequivocally stated: “The government is firmly committed to protecting future generations, including children and adolescents, from the harmful effects of tobacco and nicotine.” According to PROGGA and ATMA, initiative of a government institution to formulate a national standard for nicotine pouches is fundamentally inconsistent with the prime minister’s declared position.

item.title: Rahul Gandhi demands Narendra Modi’s resignation over protest crackdown
item.description:
India’s main opposition leader, Rahul Gandhi, demanded on Tuesday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi step down over the police crackdown against student protests demanding reforms in the education system.
Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth,” the Congress Party leader said in a post on social media as he led a march with other MPs towards the prime minister’s residence in New Delhi.
“The government doesn’t want to take any accountability, nor does it want to have a debate on it in parliament,” said Gandhi, the leader of the opposition in the lower house.
Gandhi’s comments came after police said 60 protesters were injured in clashes with security forces in the heart of New Delhi on Monday, marking the biggest street rally in the capital for about five years.
Thousands of protesters had gathered to demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following an appeal by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) online movement.
Police fired tear gas and charged with batons at protesters, who responded by pelting stones. At least 118 police personnel were also injured, Delhi Police said.
The CJP vowed to press on with its demands for Pradhan’s removal as hundreds of protesters remained camped at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protest site on Tuesday, many of them calling for changes to the wider education system.
The CJP has won millions of followers on social media since its launch in May, fueling one of the biggest challenges to Hindu-nationalist leader Modi since he won his third term in office in 2024.
“We won’t stop. Pradhan has to be sacked,” CJP spokesman Ashutosh Ranka said on social media.
There were far fewer protesters at Jantar Mantar than on Monday, when the CJP mobilized huge crowds to march on India’s parliament.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke urged protesters on Tuesday not to lose hope.
“They want to break our spirit,” he said, perched on top of a lorry. “Do not let them silence you.”
Protest organizers condemned the “high-handedness” of the authorities and said hundreds of protesters had been injured.
“It’s a shameful day in the history of Indian democracy that people, honest students, who had come for a genuine issue were brutally beaten by the Delhi police,” Ranka told AFP.
Ranka, who met senior minister JP Nadda on Monday, said the government had yet to respond to their demands.
Protesters said they would not relent.
“We have become even more fearless now,” said 25-year-old law student Chandra Pratap Sishwi.
“When I saw people being beaten up by the police like that, my blood boiled.”
Parliament was adjourned on Tuesday after the opposition benches demanded a discussion on the alleged “brutality unleashed on students.”
Despite rapid economic growth, millions of people in the world’s most populous nation still struggle to find stable and well-paying jobs, fueling discontent.
The protests follow a series of examination scandals that have shaken confidence in India’s testing system.
Some 2.2 million aspiring medical students sat for a re-examination under tight security last month after the previous test was scrapped following the leak of a question paper.
That came on top of another scandal related to the online marking of tests taken by nearly two million high school students.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju defended the government on Tuesday, saying it had acted swiftly after the exam paper leaks by arresting several people.
He said Modi had called for a “foolproof system” to prevent irregularities in the future at a closed-door meeting with his allies on Tuesday.
Modi has yet to comment directly on the protests.

item.title: Brac University, Banglacraft to strengthen Bangladesh's handicraft sector
item.description:
Brac University and the Bangladesh Handicrafts Manufacturers and Exporters Association (Banglacraft) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) at the university Tuesday, July 21 to promote entrepreneurship, innovation and sustainable growth in Bangladesh’s handicraft sector.
The MoU establishes a framework for wide-ranging collaboration spanning entrepreneurship development, capacity building, innovation, research, market access, and export promotion.
It aims to empower artisans, women entrepreneurs, and youth-led handicraft enterprises through training, mentorship, business incubation and improved access to investors and markets.
Under the agreement, the Centre for Entrepreneurship Development (CED) of Brac University will provide technical expertise in entrepreneurship development, facilitate training, mentoring and business development services, and engage Brac University faculty, researchers, and students in collaborative initiatives.
Banglacraft will facilitate access to handicraft enterprises and artisan groups, provide industry insights and sector-specific expertise, and support field-level implementation of joint activities.
Key areas of collaboration include joint training programs in business management, digital marketing, e-commerce, financial management and sustainable production practices; innovation and product development support; joint research on handicraft sector development, artisan livelihoods, market trends and export competitiveness; and entrepreneurship boot camps, business forums and networking events.
The partnership will also facilitate student internships and field engagement opportunities, creating direct industry-academia linkages.
A highlight of the collaboration will be the joint organization of an annual international crafts show Bangladesh (ICSB).
This premier platform will showcase Bangladeshi handicrafts, connect artisans with buyers, investors, and development partners, promote artisan-led enterprises and women entrepreneurs, and enhance the international visibility and export competitiveness of Bangladesh's handicraft sector.
Brac University treasurer Ariful Islam and Banglacraft president Md Belal Hossain signed the MoU.
The signing ceremony was chaired by CED head Afshana Choudhury and attended by Brac Business School dean Prof Mohammad Mujibul Haque, along with senior officials from both organizations.

item.title: RMG experts for emphasis on AI, automation & high-value products
item.description:
Industry entrepreneurs, policymakers, and experts have stressed the urgent need for Bangladesh's readymade garment (RMG) and textile sector to rapidly adopt Artificial Intelligence (AI), automated technologies, Industry 4.0, and high-value product manufacturing to maintain a competitive global standing following the country's graduation from Least Developed Country (LDC) status.
According to them, Bangladesh's future competitiveness will no longer rely solely on low production costs or tariff preferences. Instead, boosted productivity, technology-driven manufacturing, innovation, sustainable industrialization, and high value addition will form the core foundation for surviving in the global market.
Speakers shared these insights on Monday (July 20) during the opening session of the two-day "Bayla Future Summit 2026," organized by the Bangladesh Apparel Youth Leaders Alliance (Bayla) at a hotel in the capital.
Attending the event as chief guest, Minister of Labour and Employment Ariful Haque Choudhury stated that the ready-made garment industry is one of the primary drivers of the national economy and the largest employer.
To sustain long-term growth in this sector, developing skilled, innovative, and responsible next-generation leadership is essential.
He noted that upskilling and reskilling the workforce to meet the demands of technology-driven industries is a vital need of the hour. The government is actively working to implement new policy initiatives to promote sustainable industrialization and employment growth while ensuring an industry-friendly environment that balances the interests of both workers and factory owners.
Mohammad Hatem, president of the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA), remarked that the future of the apparel sector will no longer depend merely on low production costs or preferential market access. Efficiency, productivity, and the ability to adapt quickly to change will become the core strengths in competition.
Vidiya Amrit Khan, vice president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), stated that companies can no longer progress simply by manufacturing according to buyer-provided designs. Focus must shift toward innovation, original designs, brand development, and manufacturing high-value-added products.
Asif Ashraf, managing director of Urmi Group, stated that with rising wages and intensifying global competition, there is no alternative to boosting productivity, quality, and efficiency. As a result, automation is no longer a luxury, but a necessity.
He remarked: "AI will not replace humans; rather, people who use AI will replace those who do not."
Abrar Hossain Sayem, president of Bayla, said that surviving in tomorrow's global market will not be possible using traditional business models. "Think Beyond Today" is not just a slogan, but a mindset required for future competitiveness. Younger entrepreneurs must swiftly adopt AI and Industry 4.0 technologies.
Tanveer Ahmed, director of Sheltech Group, noted that Bangladesh has successfully overcome major historical challenges such as the post-quota era, global economic recessions, and the Covid-19 pandemic. To survive in the new global reality, greater investment in automation, AI, a skilled workforce, and high-value products is now required.
Nuria Lopez, chairperson of the European Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (EuroCham), observed that demand for Bangladeshi garments remains strong in the European Union market. However, maintaining this position in the future will require sustainable production, adherence to environmental standards, and product diversification. She added that next-generation entrepreneurs investing in green factories and modern technology send a positive signal for the industry.
Meanwhile, during a session titled "Scaling Beyond Manufacturing: Power of Distribution and Customer Experience," Simin Rahman, Group CEO of Transcom Limited, stated that global buyers no longer just purchase clothing—they expect quality manufacturing, sustainable operations, trust, innovation, and reliability from Bangladesh.

item.title: Prime Bank reaffirms ESG leadership with 4th consecutive Euromoney award
item.description:
Prime Bank PLC has been named “Best Bank for ESG in Bangladesh” at the prestigious Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026, marking the fourth consecutive year the bank has received this distinguished recognition.
The consecutive achievement reaffirms Prime Bank’s leadership in responsible banking and reflects its sustained commitment to integrating environmental, social and governance principles across its strategy, operations, risk-management practices and financing decisions.
Euromoney’s Awards for Excellence are regarded as a leading international benchmark of achievement in banking and finance.
The Best Bank for ESG distinction recognizes institutions demonstrating exceptional leadership in sustainable finance, responsible governance, social impact and the successful integration of ESG considerations into their business models.
Prime Bank’s recognition reflects its continued progress in strengthening ESG governance, expanding green and sustainable financing and supporting Bangladesh’s transition towards a more inclusive and climate-resilient economy.
The bank continues to promote transparent policies, robust accountability frameworks and responsible risk-management practices aligned with international standards and national sustainability priorities.
Through its sustainable finance initiatives, Prime Bank supports renewable energy, energy efficiency, environmentally responsible manufacturing and other green and transition-focused projects.
The bank also remains committed to advancing financial inclusion by improving access to finance for small and medium enterprises, women entrepreneurs, agricultural communities and underserved customer segments.
Commenting on the achievement, Faisal Rahman, chief executive officer of Prime Bank PLC, said: “Receiving this prestigious recognition from Euromoney for the fourth consecutive year is a tremendous honour. It reflects the consistency of our commitment to sustainable finance, strong governance and responsible banking. ESG is integral to how we conduct business, manage risk and create enduring value for our stakeholders.”
He added: “This achievement belongs to our employees, customers, partners and stakeholders whose trust and collective efforts continue to strengthen our sustainability journey. We remain committed to financing responsible growth and contributing to a greener, more inclusive and resilient Bangladesh.”
The recognition further strengthens Prime Bank’s resolve to pursue progress with purpose and deliver financial solutions that create meaningful economic, environmental and social impact.

item.title: Ali Afzal shares industry insights at DIU's 17th industry-academia lecture series
item.description:
To provide students with practical exposure to industry and facilitate knowledge exchange on agricultural technology and food security, Daffodil International University (DIU) organized the 17th edition of its Industry-Academia Lecture Series (IALS) on July 21 (Tuesday) at the International Conference Hall of Daffodil Smart City.
The session, titled "Post-Harvest Technology in the Field of Good Food for All," focused on post-harvest technology, food security, sustainable agriculture, and strengthening collaboration between academia and industry.
A key feature of the program was the signing of three separate Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between Krishibid Group Bangladesh (KGB) and three academic departments of DIU to promote industry-academia collaboration.
The keynote address was delivered by Prof Md Ali Afzal, founder of Krishibid Group Bangladesh, group managing director of Krishibid Group Bangladesh (KGB), and president of the Real Estate and Housing Association of Bangladesh (Rehab).
Among those present were Prof Mohammad Masum Iqbal, pro-vice chancellor of DIU; Mohammad Nadir Bin Ali, registrar; Prof SM Mahbub Ul Haque Majumder, dean; Amir Ahmed, head of the Department of Real Estate; Nizam Uddin, head of the Department of Nutrition and Food Engineering; Khandaker Moazzem Hossain, head of the Department of Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology; Md Kamruzzaman, head of the Department of Innovation and Entrepreneurship; Prof Md Belal Hossain, director of the Industrial Innovation Centre (IIC); Monowarul Islam Rebel, head of Industrial Linkage, Career Development Center (CDC); along with faculty members, students, and guests.
In his keynote address, Prof Ali Afzal highlighted the importance of effective post-harvest technologies, technological innovation in agriculture, ensuring food security, promoting sustainable farming practices, and reducing post-harvest losses.
He emphasized that close collaboration between universities and industry is essential for developing skilled human resources capable of addressing the evolving needs of Bangladesh's agricultural sector.
He also said: "Integrity, hard work, and innovative thinking are an entrepreneur's greatest strengths. In today's technology-driven world, young people have limitless opportunities. With determination, courage, and consistent effort, they can become the successful entrepreneurs of tomorrow and contribute significantly to the nation's progress."
During the program, DIU signed three separate MoUs with Krishibid Group Bangladesh involving the Department of Innovation and Entrepreneurship, the Department of Real Estate, and the Department of Nutrition and Food Engineering.
The agreements will facilitate joint research, student internships, industry-linked projects, guest lectures, workshops, and collaboration in curriculum development.

item.title: Gracie Abrams explores heartbreak and growing pains on 'Daughter From Hell'
item.description:
Gracie Abrams has released her third studio album, "Daughter From Hell," a 16-track record that explores heartbreak, identity, and the uncertainties of early adulthood through introspective songwriting.
The album marks Abrams' latest collaboration with producer Aaron Dessner and follows the success of Good Riddance (2023) and The Secret of Us (2024), which included her first UK No 1 single, That's So True.
Built around themes of responsibility, fractured relationships, and self-reflection, the album features tracks including "Good Reason," "Broke My Heart," "The Knife," and "Death Wish."
The title "Daughter From Hell" references Abrams' rebellious teenage years. Speaking to The New York Times, she said she often struggled to find her own identity while growing up and occasionally put herself in unsafe situations during her youth.
The album's production remains understated, with muted piano, soft percussion, and layered orchestration that places Abrams' vocals at the forefront. While songs such as "Hit The Wall" and "Good Reason" benefit from the minimalist approach, others, including "Humming," have drawn criticism for lacking musical urgency despite their lyrical weight.
Among the record's standout tracks are "Look At My Life," which reflects on fame and the music industry, and "Mini Bar," co-written with singer-songwriter Audrey Hobert. The title track also introduces a darker sound with distorted guitars, differing from Abrams' earlier acoustic-driven style.
The album has received praise for its emotionally candid lyrics and portrayal of early adulthood, although some critics have argued that its subdued production limits its overall impact.

In solidarity: On World Refugee Day, humanitarian actors reflect on a year of the Rohingya response
item.description:
With the number of people forcibly displaced at a record high, at a time of widespread conflict, refugees need our solidarity. Today, one in every 69 people, or 1.5% of the entire world’s population, is forcibly displaced by violence or persecution: 120 million people total. According to UNHCR’s latest Global Trends Report, the number of refugees -- people displaced across borders -- stood at a staggering 43.4 million at the year’s end, including nearly one million Rohingya refugees hosted by Bangladesh. As the Rohingya refugees await with longing their return to a stable and peaceful Myanmar, both Bangladeshi and international communities continue to demonstrate solidarity: In 2023, the Joint Response Plan for the Rohingya was among the best-funded refugee response plans globally, with 65.2% funding received against an appeal of USD 876 million. Similarly, the international community expressed its solidarity with the Rohingya refugees and the country hosting them through a record number of pledges made in December 2023 at the Global Refugee Forum in Geneva.
Hosting communities also deserve recognition and a helping hand. The generosity of the Bangladeshi people has offered the Rohingya hope in their darkest times. With empathy and shared humanity, they opened their doors and hearts -- offering safety, support and refuge. Hosting countries and communities cannot be left to do this alone. The international community must work multilaterally to create peaceful futures for all while offering refugees and hosts alike the support necessary to thrive and coexist in harmony.

The deceased were identified as Shila Akter, 25, daughter of Abdul Motaleb of Tarakanda, and Abeda Akter, 35, wife of Abdul Hamid of Raghurampur in Mymensingh Sadar Upazila. The identity of the third victim could not be known immediately immediately.
Confirming the incident, Officer-in-Charge (OC) Muhammad Shibirul Islam of Mymensingh Kotwali Model Police Station said one person died on the spot when the auto-rickshaw was run over by the truck.
He said local residents rescued four injured people and rushed them to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared two women dead on arrival.
Nazrul Islam, in-charge of the police camp at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, said three women and the auto-rickshaw driver were brought to the hospital with injuries.
"Two of the women were declared dead by the on-duty doctors. The auto-rickshaw driver received primary treatment and later left the hospital, while another woman remains admitted in critical condition," he said.
